propositions.text: Chinese couple claimed persecution as Christians and house church members
propositions.quote: This judicial review concerns a Chinese couple who claimed to be persecuted because they are Christians and members of a “house” church.

propositions.text: RPD denied refugee application due to lack of credibility and implausibility
propositions.quote: The Refugee Protection Division [RPD], on the basis of lack of credibility and the implausibility of their story, denied their refugee/protection application.

paragraphs.summary: Court states Chinese couple claimed persecution as Christians; RPD denied application for lack of credibility and implausibility.

propositions.text: Applicants introduced to faith by Ms Xu and joined underground church in 2009
propositions.quote: The Applicants claim that their friend, a Ms Xu, introduced them to the faith and took them to her underground Protestant church in the Shandong Province, China.

propositions.text: Applicants visited son in Canada two years later and joined a church there
propositions.quote: Two years later, the Applicants visited their son in Canada where they joined a church.

propositions.text: This forms basis of sur place claim
propositions.quote: This is the basis of the sur place part of their claim.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants say Ms Xu introduced them to faith and underground church; they visited son in Canada and joined church, basis for sur place claim.

propositions.text: Applicants claim Ms Xu arrested and PSB looking for them after arrival in Canada
propositions.quote: Subsequent to their arrival in Canada, the Applicants claim that Ms Xu has been arrested and the Public Security Bureau [PSB] has been looking for them.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants claim Ms Xu arrested and PSB looking for them after they arrived in Canada.

propositions.text: RPD did not find conversion narrative credible
propositions.quote: In the RPD’s decision, the Member did not find the narrative of their conversion to be credible.

propositions.text: RPD found implausible that Ms Xu revealed illegal church membership given persecution
propositions.quote: She found implausible that Ms Xu readily revealed her membership in an illegal church given that Christians were facing significant persecution in Shandong Province.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found Applicants' conversion story not credible and Ms Xu revealing illegal church membership implausible.

propositions.text: RPD acknowledged documents corroborating Christian practice in Canada
propositions.quote: The RPD acknowledged the documents corroborating the Applicants’ practice of Christianity in Canada

propositions.text: Due to credibility concerns about China events, RPD did not find documents conclusive of faith
propositions.quote: because of credibility concerns of the narrative of events in China, the Member did not find such documents and activities to be conclusive of their faith.

paragraphs.summary: RPD accepted documents showing Christian practice in Canada but did not find them conclusive due to credibility concerns about China events.

propositions.text: RPD found PSB pursuit narrative implausible because PSB would know Applicants were in Canada
propositions.quote: The RPD also found that the narrative of being pursued by the PSB to be implausible because the PSB would know from its database that the Applicants were in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found story of PSB pursuing Applicants implausible as PSB would know they were in Canada.

propositions.text: RPD accepted house churches could be persecuted but targeted individuals tend to be leaders
propositions.quote: the Member accepted that house churches could, in some places, be subject to persecution; however, targeted individuals tended to be leaders

propositions.text: Applicants did not establish serious possibility of persecution given many Christian practitioners
propositions.quote: the Applicants had not established a serious possibility that they would be persecuted.

paragraphs.summary: RPD accepted house churches may face persecution but Applicants not likely targeted as they are not leaders.

propositions.text: Credibility findings reviewed for reasonableness; burden of proof legal test is correctness standard
propositions.quote: a) the interpretation and assessment of evidence (particularly credibility findings) are subject to the reasonableness standard of review and b) that the legal test for burden of proof attracts a correctness standard.

paragraphs.summary: Court states credibility findings reviewed for reasonableness; burden of proof legal test reviewed for correctness.

propositions.text: Applicants argue RPD erred using term 'conclusive evidence' of faith
propositions.quote: The Applicants have attempted to make a legal issue out of terms such as “conclusive evidence” of their faith.

propositions.text: RPD focused on correct legal test despite some questionable wording
propositions.quote: while there is some questionable wording, the RPD was focused on the correct legal test in this case.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue RPD erred on 'conclusive evidence' wording; court finds RPD applied correct legal test overall.

propositions.text: Decision must be quashed due to inadequate articulation of implausibility findings
propositions.quote: this decision must be quashed on other grounds. Findings of credibility are accorded considerable deference but implausibility findings require a more rigorous standard, a clear articulation of the basis for a finding of implausibility

paragraphs.summary: Court quashes decision because implausibility findings lack clear articulation and record support.

propositions.text: Comments on facts limited as matter remitted to RPD for new determination
propositions.quote: my comments on the facts and what can be drawn from them must be limited.

paragraphs.summary: Court limits factual comments since matter is remitted to RPD for new decision.

propositions.text: Implausibility conclusions without record basis are arbitrary and unreasonable
propositions.quote: A conclusion that a matter is implausible without articulation of the basis in the record (rather than just some personal opinion) is arbitrary and unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds implausibility conclusions without record basis are arbitrary and unreasonable.

propositions.text: RPD did not explain PSB not looking for Applicants beyond speculation about database use
propositions.quote: The RPD did not explain the finding that the PSB was not looking for the Applicants other than to suggest that the PSB could have used their database to find them.

propositions.text: This speculation is unreasonable given evidence of persecution of house church members in Shandong
propositions.quote: This was pure speculation especially in light of the significant evidence that there was persecution of house church members in Shandong Province.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD's PSB not looking for Applicants finding speculative and unreasonable given persecution evidence.

propositions.text: RPD inconsistently discounts Ms Xu story due to PSB threat then says PSB unlikely interested in Applicants
propositions.quote: On the one hand, the RPD discounts the Applicants’ story of the meeting and actions of Ms Xu because of the threat of the PSB and then later concludes that the PSB is not likely to be looking for or interested in the Applicants.

propositions.text: RPD's reasoning is difficult to follow
propositions.quote: It is difficult to follow the RPD’s line of reasoning.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD's reasoning inconsistent and difficult to follow regarding PSB threat and interest in Applicants.

propositions.text: RPD failed to consider persecution of house church members
propositions.quote: The RPD did not consider whether there was persecution of house church members.

propositions.text: Freedom of religion includes public worship, spreading gospel, bearing witness
propositions.quote: freedom of religion includes the right to go public, the right to spread the gospel, and the right to bear witness.

propositions.text: RPD should have considered house churches as modern catacombs
propositions.quote: The RPD should have considered whether the house churches are today’s version of the catacombs.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD failed to consider house church persecution; cites law on religious freedom and suggests house churches as modern catacombs.

propositions.text: RPD gave cursory consideration to sur place claim after dismissing China events claim
propositions.quote: Having dismissed the refugee/protection claim based on events in China, the RPD had an obligation to consider the sur place claim. It gave it such cursory consideration as to fail to properly consider that claim.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD failed to properly consider sur place claim after dismissing China events claim.

propositions.text: Judicial review granted, RPD decision quashed, matter remitted to RPD for new decision by different panel
propositions.quote: this judicial review will be granted, the RPD’s decision quashed and the matter remitted to the RPD for a new decision by a different panel.

paragraphs.summary: Court grants judicial review, quashes RPD decision, and remits matter to RPD for new decision by different panel.

propositions.text: No question for certification; judgment grants judicial review, quashes RPD decision, remits matter to RPD
propositions.quote: There is no question for certification. JUDGMENT THIS COURT’S JUDGMENT is that the application for judicial review is granted, the Refugee Protection Division’s decision is quashed and the matter is to be remitted to the Refugee Protection Division for a new decision by a different panel.

paragraphs.summary: Court states no certification question; judgment grants review, quashes RPD decision, remits matter to RPD.
